title: Access Governance Routing: Decision Heuristic and Intake Consolidation for Enterprise Admin Requests
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers submit a high volume of admin & access requests (RBAC, SSO/SAML, SCIM, org policy changes). Current intake is noisy: inconsistent fields, duplicated tickets, and manual routing to product, infra, or security. That causes SLA misses and lost visibility into enterprise onboarding blockers.

Goal: Replace ad hoc routing with a deterministic decision heuristic that classifies and prioritizes requests on intake so they are routed to the correct team, assigned an SLA, and surfaced to the customer with clear next steps. The solution should reduce manual triage time, lower mean time to resolution for high-impact access requests, and enable analytics for prioritization trends.

Scope: This ticket covers the PM-side design of the heuristic, the intake form schema, acceptance criteria, rollout plan, and high-level analytics/KPI definitions. Engineering tickets for implementation (API, queueing, UI) are in ENG-2892 and ENG-3045. Security will review the rubric for regulatory flags.

Out-of-scope: Deep RBAC policy simulation, SCIM connector implementation, and full self-serve admin console UX refresh (these are separate initiatives).
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic scoring rubric is documented and reviewed by Security and SRE
Intake schema (fields + validations) is finalized and linked in this ticket
Routing map from score ranges to queues (self-serve, PM triage, security review, enterprise onboarding) is defined
SLA tiers are assigned to each routing outcome and documented
Example evaluation: provide 5 representative historical tickets mapped to expected routing and priority
Telemetry spec created: events, metrics, and dashboard requirements for tracking volume, latency, and misroutes
notes: We must support both API-based intake (internal SRE automation, partner integrations) and UI intake (support portal).
Keep the heuristic explainable so customer success can justify routing decisions to customers.
Avoid binary rules that create hot paths (e.g., everything with 'SSO' text automatically escalates) — combine signals.
Coordinate with Growth for any self-serve changes that impact free trial flows.
Retention of audit trail: every routing decision must be stored with the scoring breakdown for later review.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): Wire intake schema into support portal + internal API and enable heuristic with logging only for two large customers (canary); Phase 2: Enable automatic routing for low-risk score bands (self-serve docs and automated responses); Phase 3: Enable full routing with SLA assignments and begin reporting; Phase 4: Expand to all customers and retire legacy manual routing spreadsheet.
metrics: Mean time to first response (MTTR) by routing bucket
Percentage of requests auto-routed vs manual
Misroute rate (human override after automated routing)
Volume by request subtype (RBAC, SSO, SCIM, org-policy)
Backlog size for PM triage queue
